cards.text: Big battle shaping up, friend. The Philistines bring all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camps by the spring in Jezreel. Meanwhile David and his men have been living in Philistine territory under Achish, king of Gath (1 Samuel 27:2-7).

cards.question: The Philistine leaders march out in units of hundreds and thousands. Who's marching behind them with Achish?

cards.text: The Philistine commanders spot David's crew in the line and ask, “What about these Hebrews?” Friend, that's the look you give when somebody nobody recognizes shows up in your team photo.

cards.question: Achish speaks up for David. True or false: he tells the commanders he's found no fault in David from the day he defected until today.

cards.text: The commanders are not convinced, not even a little bit. They're ANGRY with Achish.

cards.question: What do the angry Philistine commanders tell Achish to do with David?

answers.text: Send him back where you assigned him
Put him at the front of the battle
Keep him under guard in the camp

cards.question: The commanders say David must not go down into battle with them, only to become their ___ during the war.

cards.text: They figure there's no better way for David to win back his master's favor than with the heads of their men. Friend, that is ONE way to get your old job back.

cards.question: The commanders back up their worry with a song people sing about David in their dances. What does the song say?

answers.text: Saul has slain his thousands and David his tens of thousands
Saul is our king and David is our mighty shield
David has won the day and Saul has won the war

cards.text: So Achish calls David in and tells him, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright, and it seems right in my sight that you should march in and out with me in the army,”

cards.question: True or false: Achish tells David that the Philistine leaders see him as good too.
So what does Achish tell David to do, so he won't displease the Philistine leaders?

answers.text: Turn back now and go in peace
Stay in camp and guard the supplies
March at the front with the leaders

cards.text: David pushes back: “But what have I done?” Friend, that's the face of a man who showed up early, worked hard, and still got sent home before his shift even started.

cards.question: David asks Achish what he's found against him to keep him from going along to fight against the ___ of his lord the king.

cards.text: Achish tells David he's as pleasing in his sight as an angel of God. But the commanders have spoken: he must not go into battle with them.

cards.question: Achish gives David his orders: get up ___ in the morning with the men who came with you, and go as soon as it is ___.
Next morning, David and his men are up early. Where are they headed?

answers.text: Back to the land of the Philistines
Over to Saul's camp at Gilboa

cards.question: True or false: after David leaves, the Philistines go up to Jezreel.

cards.text: The Philistines march one way, and David marches the other. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, but this story's got plenty of road left.

findings.problem: The joke compares the commanders to people looking at 'somebody nobody recognizes' in a team photo. The commanders aren't confused about who these men are. They call them Hebrews (29:3), and in 29:5 they name David and quote the song about him. They are suspicious of someone they know, not puzzled by a stranger. So the everyday comparison doesn't share the core action. It also hints at something the text shows isn't so, that they don't recognize him.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says David and his men have been living under Achish. Card 2 then asks who is marching behind the Philistines with Achish. The two wrong answers are Saul's own men, Jonathan and Abner, and the setup has just placed Israel in a separate camp at Jezreel. So the setup rules out both wrong answers, and the pick is a giveaway rather than an informed guess.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
